alt: Line chart on a dark background: share of faults found versus fault size relative to the detection threshold. Vibration, battery sag and GNSS dropout curves rise from near 0% at half the threshold to 100% at twice it.
post:
A drone flight log holds hundreds of signals. After a bad flight, the hard part is finding the minute that matters.

I built an open-source triage tool for PX4 ULog files. One command gives a ranked list of problems with timestamps and a one-page report: vibration and accelerometer clipping, battery sag and internal resistance, GNSS loss, estimator rejections, RC and telemetry loss, motor saturation, CPU load. Every threshold is documented and configurable.

To measure it, I took 70 public logs from the PX4 Flight Review database and injected known faults into their signals:
- At twice the detection threshold, 100% of vibration bursts, voltage sags and GNSS dropouts were found.
- Median timing error was 0.1-0.3 s.
- On 20 held-out logs that their uploaders rated good, it raised 7.2 fault flags per flight hour, and 16 of the 20 logs had none.
- It processes 3.6 MB of log per second on one thread.

Not verified yet: no hardware, thresholds are not tuned per airframe, and real-log labels are the uploader's rating plus my own hand check.

If you review flight logs, which flag would save you the most time?

Code: https://github.com/VB-Builds/px4-flightlog-triage
